name: Scholar
body:
You are a person of great intellect, dedicated to the study of multiple fields and the acquisition of esoteric lore. You seek knowledge in all its forms, both mundane and arcane, always working toward the goal of better understanding the multiverse.

There are many traditional fields of knowledge available for scholarly pursuit, although you start with expertise in only a few, and it is rare that any scholar has the skill to truly master more than a handful of subjects. While scholars like you are widely regarded for their knowledge, many also see you as aloof and mysterious—a champion of radical concepts or antiquated institutions, whose motives are not well understood.

In truth, your pursuits are almost strictly academic, not tied to any religious or arcane tradition, and as such you maintain an official position of neutrality in all affairs—loyal only to knowledge in its purest form.

Role: Scholars are very versatile, able to perform a wide variety of functions and support a wide variety of roles—depending on their fields of study. However, while scholars have a very wide breadth of knowledge, they are only able to truly master a narrow band of knowledge.

Hit Die: d8.
Starting Age: Trained.
Starting Wealth: 3d6 × 10 (average 105 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.
Class Skills

Your class skills (and the key ability for each skill) are: Appraise (Int), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Knowledge (all) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 6 + Int modifier.

Table: The Scholar

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the scholar class.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

You are proficient with all simple weapons and with light armor, but not with shields.

Inspiration (Ex)

You possess keen powers of observation and deduction that far surpass the abilities of others. You typically use these powers to aid in your studies, but can also use these flashes of inspiration in other situations.

You have the ability to augment skill checks and ability checks through your brilliant inspiration. You have an inspiration pool equal to 1/2 your scholar level (minimum 1) + your Intelligence modifier. Your inspiration pool refreshes each day after a long rest. As a free action, you can expend one use of inspiration from your pool to add 1d6 to the result of the check, including any on which you take 10 or 20.

This choice is made after the check is rolled and before the results are revealed. You can only use inspiration once per check or roll.

You can use inspiration on any skill that you have selected with your studies class feature without expending a use of inspiration from your pool.

Inspiration can also be used on attack rolls and saving throws, but at the cost of expending two uses of inspiration each time from your pool. In the case of saving throws, using inspiration is a reaction rather than a free action.

If you gain the inspiration feature from another source, you add your pools together, but you only add your Intelligence modifier once.

Scholar’s Notebook: As you acquire new knowledge, you must keep notes regarding what you have learned. The typical scholar’s notebook is the dimensions of a wizard’s spellbook, although this is only a guideline and may vary from scholar to scholar.

Every day after you complete 8 hours of sleep, you must review your notes for one hour, or else your inspiration pool is reduced by 2 points for that day (to a minimum of 1 point). Alternately, you can study in a library that contains scholarly tomes related to your fields of study.

If you lose your notebook, you can recreate it with 8 hours of work, as well as special inks and papers costing 100 gp per level.

You may even create multiple copies of your notebook in this way, but only you are able to read your notes well enough to garner useful knowledge from them.

Scholar Studies

At 1st level, choose any two of the 15 traditional scholar fields of study:

Alchemy
Arcana
Astrology
Economics
Engineering
Geography
Heraldry
History
Horticulture
Jurisprudence
Linguistics
Medicine
Ravenry
Smithing
Warcraft

You must be trained (minimum 1 rank) in the associated skills for whatever studies you choose. You gain the basic study ability for each of your chosen studies. At 3rd level and every 3 levels thereafter, choose one additional study whose prerequisite you meet, and gain its associated basic study ability.

At 2nd level and every level thereafter, you also gain an advanced study ability. To select an advanced study ability, you must first have selected the basic study ability for that field of study. You must also meet any additional prerequisites listed for the advanced study ability chosen. Unless otherwise noted, each study ability can only be selected once.

Techniques

While you are not typically a front-line combatant, your studies often give you a tactical advantage during combat. You gain access to various combat techniques with each new field of study you select with your scholar studies class feature. You can select one of these associated techniques at 1st level and an additional one at 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter.

You can use a move action to study a single enemy that you can see. After doing so, you gain a window of time equal to your Intelligence bonus in rounds (minimum 1 round). Choose any one of your techniques, which then becomes active against that opponent during that window. Once the duration has ended, you can spend another move action to study an opponent and gain a new window of time. You can also change targets or techniques at any time by spending another move action, which immediately ends the previous technique and begins a new one.

At 8th level, you can activate this ability as either a swift action or a move action. At 16th level, you can activate it as a free action, allowing you to freely alternate between targets and techniques.

True Inspiration (Ex)

At 20th level, you add 1d6 on all ability checks and skill checks without expending a point of inspiration from your pool—including skills you aren’t trained in.

In addition, whenever you do expend inspiration on an ability check, attack roll, saving throw, or skill check, you add 2d6 rather than 1d6 to the result.

Favored Class Bonuses
Android Add a +1/2 bonus on Knowledge (engineering) checks and a +1/2 bonus to Appraise checks made on technological items.
Drow Add a +1/2 bonus on Knowledge (arcana) checks and a +1/2 bonus on Bluff checks made to pass a secret message.
Dwarf Add a +1/2 bonus on Knowledge (dungeoneering) checks and a +1/2 bonus on Perception checks made underground.
Elf Add +1/4 point to your inspiration pool.
Gnome Gain +1/5 of a new basic study.
Half-Elf Add a +1/3 to your inspiration rolls.
Halfling Add a +1/2 bonus on Knowledge (local) checks and a +1/2 bonus on Diplomacy checks made to gather information.
Half-orc Gain +1/6 of a new technique.
Human Gain +1/6 of a new advanced study.
Kasatha Add a +1/2 bonus on Knowledge (history) checks and a +1/2 bonus on Acrobatics checks made to jump.
Lashunta Add a +1/2 bonus on Knowledge (nature) checks and a +1/2 bonus on Diplomacy checks made to gather information.
Ratfolk Add a +1/2 bonus on Craft (alchemy) checks and a +1/2 bonus on Handle Animal checks.
Samsaran Gain +1/5 of a new basic study.
Shirren Add a +1/2 bonus on Heal checks and a +1/2 bonus on Profession (soldier) checks.
Vesk Add a +1 bonus to your CMD when resisting a sunder attempt, and a +1/2 bonus on Profession (soldier) checks.
Wayang Add a +1/2 bonus on Knowledge (planes) checks and a +1/2 bonus on Perception checks made in conditions of dim light or darkness.
Ysoki Gain +1/6 of a new advanced study.
Variant Multiclassing

You gain the following benefits:

3rd level: Scholar Inspiration
7th level: Scholar Basic Study
11th level: Scholar Advanced Study
15th level: Scholar Technique
19th level: Scholar Advanced Technique (2nd)
Variant Multiclassing Feats
Scholar Basic Study (VMC)

Prerequisite(s): character level 3rd, see description.

Benefit(s): You gain a basic study ability. You must have at least 1 rank in the associated skill for the basic study you choose. If the ability requires the use of inspiration, you must have the scholar inspiration feat as a prerequisite. You use your character level as your effective scholar level for the purposes of this ability.

Special: You may choose this feat a second time at 7th level, a third time at 11th level, and a fourth time at 15th level.

Scholar Inspiration (VMC)

Prerequisite(s): no levels in a class that has the inspiration class feature, character level 3rd.

Benefit(s): You gain the scholar’s inspiration class feature, with a pool of inspiration equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1). For every additional scholar dedication feat you possess, add 1 additional point of inspiration to your pool.

You can use inspiration on any skill for which you have the corresponding Scholar Basic Study feat without expending a use of inspiration.

Scholar Technique (VMC)

Prerequisite(s): Scholar Basic Study, character level 7th, see description.

Benefit(s): You gain a technique ability. You must have the basic study for whatever technique you choose, and you use your character level as your effective scholar level. If the technique requires the use of inspiration, you must have the scholar inspiration feat as a prerequisite.

Special: You may choose this feat a second time at 15th level.

Scholar Advanced Study (VMC)

Prerequisite(s): Scholar Basic Study, character level 11th, see description.

Benefit(s): You gain an advanced study ability.

You must meet the prerequisites for whatever ability you choose, using your character level as your scholar level. If the ability requires the use of inspiration, you must have the scholar inspiration feat as a prerequisite.

Special: You may choose this feat a second time at 19th level.
